title: Resonance Sellflow — Field Deck (draft)
summary: Working draft of a compact field-facing sell deck + two compact battlecards focused on helping sellers rapidly create urgency around latency/cost predictability and operational resilience. Intentionally short, with scripted micro-narratives per persona and a rapid pilot checklist tailored to platform/infra buyers.
slide_outline: Cover: Resonance Sellflow — 6 minute field deck (what we want the customer to remember)
Why inference economics matter now: 3 signals (model variance, token tail, burstiness)
Customer problem frame: unpredictable tail latency, surprise costs, and fragmented deployment options
Redwood in one line: a single runtime + policies that make inference predictable across hosted, dedicated and private
Throughput Confidence Index (TCI): visual showing expected latency and cost bands for small/med/large workloads
Persona vignettes (integration architect, platform owner, product PM) — 30s scripts and one ask each
Decision friction map: 3 common blockers and the one-sentence retort for each
Proof points: 2 anonymized pilot outcomes and an ops rescue example
Pilot promise: 3-step zero-regret pilot plan (15 day technical pilot, fallback policy, cost baseline)
Next steps and call-to-action: technical handoff, pilot success metric, sketch SOW
speaker_notes: Keep slides conversational — spend most time on persona vignettes and the pilot promise. Avoid deep infra benchmarking numbers in first meeting; instead offer an immediate live-run to show the TCI on their sample workload. Use the decision friction map to preempt legal/procurement questions and keep the conversation focused on deployability and observability.
battlecards: Integration Architect — 45s pitch: Focus on latency predictability. Say: 'We turn bursty request patterns into stable tail latency using continuous batching + KV prefix caching; you can pin a model and a fallback policy so your UI never drops to a 10s wait unexpectedly.' Quick objections: 'We can't change model' -> 'You don't have to — pin current version and use an isolated variant for canary. We route automatically.' Technical ask: sample trace and a 24-hour request histogram.

Platform Owner — 60s pitch: Emphasize capacity economics and SLAs. Say: 'Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved throughput with burst lanes and contractual latency bands so you stop overprovisioning. Our billing ties to throughput tiers and token units so finance has predictable run-rate.' Quick objections: 'Procurement won't sign another contract' -> 'Offer pilot-to-purchase path: 30-day eval on a usage-based credit, then negotiate a short reserved window if the ROI is proven.' Technical ask: baseline QPS and expected peak window for a 1-week period.

CTO / Head of Product — 45s pitch: Risk and feature velocity. Say: 'You get a unified API across hosted and private deployments, so experiments move to production without re-architecting. We instrument cost and quality per-prompt so you can test model upgrades with guardrails.' Quick objections: 'Open models are cheaper' -> 'We recommend model mix + quantization profiles; hosting costs are one input — operational availability and rollback speed are where most outages/bad UX come from.' Technical ask: define an MVP feature and a success metric (latency at p95, cost per 1k calls, quality recall on a small eval set).
decision_friction_map: Blocker: Unclear cost delta across pilots — Retort: We'll run your sample traffic and return a per-feature cost delta with 95% confidence intervals within 48 hours.
Blocker: Security/compliance concerns for regulated data — Retort: We can run a private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs; initial pilot can use synthetic or redacted payloads.
Blocker: Team bandwidth to integrate — Retort: 2-week lightweight integration (serverless SDK + platform plugin), plus a dedicated SE check-in and runbook template.

Blocker: Fear of model regressions after switching — Retort: We keep model versioning + automated quality regression alerts tied to an eval set; you decide rollout speed and automatic fallback thresholds.
pilot_checklist: Day 0: Align on success metrics (p95 latency target, cost ceiling per 10k requests, and quality gate on a 50-example eval)
Day 1-3: Provide sample traffic + small eval prompts. Redwood seeds a TCI run and returns expected latency/cost bands.
Day 4-8: Live-run on subset (shadow or 5% traffic) with tracing hooks and SLO dashboard access.
Day 9-12: Joint review, tweak batching/quantization profiles, and configure fallback policies for peak windows.
Day 13-15: Finalize handoff, export runbook and cost forecast, recommend commit path for Dedicated or Private deployment.
proof_points: Pilot A (fintech): Reduced tail latency variance by 3x on bursty morning windows, enabling a real-time fraud-check feature to ship without re-architecting.
Pilot B (SaaS search): Cut per-query token cost by 22% using quantization + prefix caching; SLA compliance reduced incident MTTR by 45%.
Ops Rescue: During a model rollout that introduced increased latency p99, automatic fallbacks kept the customer UI within SLO while the model was rolled back.
ask_and_next_steps: Ask: Get 1 week of representative logs and pick a 2-week pilot window. Next: technical handshake with SE + 15 minute calendar block for alignment, then a concrete SOW draft if pilot metrics meet thresholds.
notes_to_self: - Keep the deck under 12 slides. - Bring an anonymized TCI chart for a live demo. - Prep 3 short customer anecdotes tied to each persona. - Coordinate with legal on the pilot terms one week before demo.
audience_advice: Use this deck for early technical qualification calls and short field demos. For procurement-heavy accounts, pre-send the pilot checklist and a lightweight SOW template to reduce friction.

raw_body:
RES: Short field deck for seller-enablement

Open: 30s framing script
- 'Most teams we talk to are blocked by unpredictable inference costs or occasional spikes that break UX. Redwood helps you make inference predictable so you can ship features without building a bespoke serving stack.'

Persona scripts (copyable):
- Integration Architect: 'If you can share a 24hr trace, we can show the TCI for your workload and a suggested fallback policy in 48h.'
- Platform Owner: 'Reserve a burst lane for seasonal peaks; we'll model the cost delta so you can choose commit levels confidently.'
- CTO: 'We help you run experiments and roll them to production with the same runtime — fewer rollbacks, faster feature cycles.'

Objection snippets (one-liners):
- 'We're worried about vendor lock' -> 'You keep model ownership and can run Private; API contracts are simple JSON and we provide migration runbooks.'
- 'What about open-source models?' -> 'Open models aren't free when you consider engineering ops; Redwood optimizes unit economics plus gives operational reliability.'

Appendix material to share after call: Pilot checklist (one-pager), SOW sketch (two paragraphs), lightweight security brief (KMS + audit logs).
